business_question: Did “women and children first” apply on the Titanic? Compare survival rates for adult women, children under 16, and adult men across passenger classes. Exclude passengers with missing ages from these age-defined groups and state this limitation.
business_answer_shown: The survival outcomes are consistent with a women-and-children-first pattern across all three passenger classes: adult women and children under 16 had higher survival rates than adult men in every class. Passenger class still mattered substantially; in 3rd class fewer than half of adult women (46.1%) and children (40.5%) survived, although both rates remained above the adult-men rate of 15.0%. These descriptive survival patterns do not by themselves establish evacuation policy or causation.

baseline_chart_assessment.issue: The baseline title describes the plotted categories but does not directly communicate the answer to the business question.
baseline_chart_assessment.why_it_matters: A management audience must infer the principal finding by comparing nine bars rather than seeing the decision-relevant message immediately.
baseline_chart_assessment.related_principle: Method - Title; Story - Visual Story; Purpose - Frame

baseline_chart_assessment.issue: Group identity requires repeated lookup between the legend and bars.
baseline_chart_assessment.why_it_matters: The audience must move its eyes between the legend and three differently colored series across all passenger classes, adding cognitive load to the central comparison.

baseline_chart_assessment.issue: Three equally prominent series colors do not create a clear hierarchy and make color carry more identification work than necessary.
baseline_chart_assessment.why_it_matters: The important evidence is the magnitude of the survival-rate differences, not the palette. Direct category labeling can communicate group identity without relying on color.

baseline_chart_assessment.issue: The vertical grouped layout is accurate but separates group names from the individual marks and requires more back-and-forth scanning than necessary.
baseline_chart_assessment.why_it_matters: A horizontal arrangement can place complete group labels adjacent to each value while preserving the same zero-based quantitative comparison.
baseline_chart_assessment.related_principle: Charts - Right Chart and Selection; Perception - Mind

data_fidelity_checks.check: Recalculated all nine survival rates and denominators from the supplied spreadsheet using the specified age and sex definitions.
data_fidelity_checks.notes: 1st class: adult women 126/130 = 96.9%, children 7/8 = 87.5%, adult men 48/146 = 32.9%. 2nd class: adult women 76/87 = 87.4%, children 27/28 = 96.4%, adult men 12/146 = 8.2%. 3rd class: adult women 53/115 = 46.1%, children 32/79 = 40.5%, adult men 46/307 = 15.0%. These match the baseline chart.

data_fidelity_checks.check: Verified treatment of missing age values.
data_fidelity_checks.notes: 263 of 1,309 passenger records have missing age, equal to 20.1%. They are excluded from all age-defined groups as required.

data_fidelity_checks.check: Verified cohort definitions and coverage of records with known age.
data_fidelity_checks.notes: Children are age under 16 regardless of sex; adult women are female age 16+; adult men are male age 16+. The cohorts contain 115 children, 332 adult women, and 599 adult men, totaling all 1,046 passengers with known age.

data_fidelity_checks.check: Verified scale and ordering preserve quantitative relationships.
data_fidelity_checks.notes: The improved chart uses one common survival-rate scale beginning at zero, preserves passenger-class order from 1st through 3rd, and preserves the adult-women, children, adult-men comparison within each class.

principles_applied.change_made: Replaced the descriptive title with the answer-oriented title 'Women and children had higher survival rates than adult men in every passenger class' and added a subtitle highlighting the materially weaker 3rd-class outcomes.
principles_applied.expected_communication_benefit: The principal evidence is understandable immediately instead of requiring the audience to infer the conclusion from nine separate bars.

principles_applied.change_made: Removed the separate legend and placed the group names directly beside their corresponding bars.
principles_applied.expected_communication_benefit: Reduces legend lookup and makes category identity unambiguous without dependence on color.

principles_applied.change_made: Grouped the three cohorts together within each passenger class, inserted visual spacing between classes, and kept one aligned quantitative scale.
principles_applied.expected_communication_benefit: Reduces mental reconstruction and makes within-class and across-class comparisons easier to scan.

principles_applied.change_made: Used a restrained single-series visual treatment, removed the legend, reduced non-data elements, and retained only light reference gridlines.
principles_applied.expected_communication_benefit: Improves signal-to-noise ratio and ensures the chart remains interpretable without relying on multiple colors.

principles_applied.change_made: Retained the bar-chart family because the task is a categorical rate comparison, but changed from vertical grouped columns to horizontal class-grouped bars to accommodate direct descriptive labels.
principles_applied.expected_communication_benefit: Preserves accurate zero-based magnitude comparison while materially reducing eye movement and label ambiguity.

principles_applied.change_made: Preserved the missing-age limitation, age definitions, sample sizes, and added a note distinguishing observed survival outcomes from proof of evacuation policy or causation.
principles_applied.expected_communication_benefit: Keeps the visualization closely tied to the supplied business question without overstating what the available data can establish.

improved_chart.chart_type: Horizontal bar chart with rows grouped by passenger class
improved_chart.title: Women and children had higher survival rates than adult men in every passenger class
improved_chart.accessibility_notes: The chart uses direct text labels and does not require a legend or color discrimination to identify groups. Percentages and sample sizes are printed beside each bar, all rates share a common zero-based scale, and the missing-age limitation is stated visibly. Artifact: improved_chart.png

baseline_to_improved_comparison.baseline: The viewer sees accurate survival-rate differences, but the neutral title leaves the main conclusion to be inferred.
baseline_to_improved_comparison.improved: The title states the central descriptive finding immediately, while the subtitle highlights the important 3rd-class qualification.

baseline_to_improved_comparison.baseline: Three colors and a separate legend identify the cohorts.
baseline_to_improved_comparison.improved: Cohort names appear directly beside the bars, eliminating legend lookup and reducing reliance on color.

baseline_to_improved_comparison.baseline: The chart contains the required groups and missing-age note but frames the display primarily as a generic comparison.
baseline_to_improved_comparison.improved: The framing directly addresses whether survival outcomes show a women-and-children-first pattern and preserves the key limitation.

baseline_to_improved_comparison.baseline: The grouped columns require repeated horizontal scanning among bars, legend entries, percentages, and sample sizes.
baseline_to_improved_comparison.improved: Class-grouped horizontal rows align labels, bars, rates, and sample sizes, reducing cognitive load and making the comparison structure more explicit.

baseline_to_improved_comparison.baseline: The descriptive title, three-color palette, legend, and grid structure give secondary design elements substantial visual weight.
baseline_to_improved_comparison.improved: The answer-oriented title, restrained treatment, light gridlines, direct labels, and removal of the legend increase the signal-to-noise ratio.

baseline_to_improved_comparison.baseline: A grouped bar chart is an appropriate categorical-comparison form and the underlying quantitative encoding is accurate.
baseline_to_improved_comparison.improved: The bar-chart family is retained rather than changed gratuitously; horizontal orientation materially improves direct labeling while preserving the same evidence and zero baseline.

remaining_limitations: The source data contain survival outcomes but do not directly measure evacuation instructions or boarding sequence, so the chart cannot prove that a women-and-children-first policy caused the observed differences.

The 263 passengers with missing ages, representing 20.1% of records, cannot be assigned to the required age-defined cohorts; their exclusion may affect how completely the chart represents all passengers.
The 1st-class children group contains only 8 passengers, so its 87.5% descriptive survival rate is based on a much smaller denominator than most other groups.
The chart reports descriptive rates and sample sizes only; it does not display statistical uncertainty.
